subject: Discovery recap: reliability & graceful degradation - Acme Retail
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: reliability & graceful degradation - Acme Retail

Sarah, thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we're aligned.

Key pain points you shared:
- Production incidents in Q4 2025 where the in-house model endpoint went down during peak traffic (Black Friday peak); degraded responses and multi-hour recovery.
- Lack of predictable SLAs for inference latency and availability; hard to commit guarantees to internal product stakeholders.
- No transparent routing/fallback strategy — when primary region is constrained, the app loses the LLM feature entirely.

Current stack you described:
- Core product hosted in us-west-2 on AWS; in-house model on a GPU pool managed by your infra team.
- Redis cache for session state, Postgres for user metadata.
- No dedicated multi-region inference setup today; manual failover.

Success criteria you mentioned:
- 99.9% inference availability for critical endpoints with documented SLOs/SLA options.
- Automatic graceful degradation: user-facing fallbacks (lower-cost model variants, cached completions, or static templates) so UX degrades predictably rather than failing.
- Clear post-incident timelines and root-cause info for exec reporting.

What we can help with (high level):
- Dedicated or private deployment options with SLA-backed uptime and predictable latency targets.
- Smart routing & fallback: automatic region and model variant routing + cache-first behaviors to preserve UX.
- Incident tracing and audit logs for each request plus runbook integration.

Proposed next steps:
1) Share a concise incident log for your most recent outage (I've attached a suggested CSV template — feel free to attach your file).
2) We'll prepare an SLA draft and a short technical note on fallback strategies (attached: SLA-draft-20260218.pdf and rdw-product-one-pager.pdf).
3) Technical follow-up call: 60 min with your infra + product to walk architecture and map a Mutual Action Plan (MAP). Suggested time slots: Feb 23 or Feb 25.
4) If procurement is engaged, we can scope Dedicated capacity pricing and procurement playbook.

Quick ask: can you confirm who from infra will join the follow-up (you mentioned Michael Lee) and whether a procurement contact should be included? Also, if you can attach the incident timeline (start/end, P1/P2/P3 flags) that'll help us scope fallback windows.

Attaching:
- SLA-draft-20260218.pdf (draft SLA options)
- incident-log-2025-Q4.csv (template/example)
- rdw-product-one-pager.pdf

Thanks — I'll hold Feb 23 and 25 windows until I hear back.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0147

From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acmeretail.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 17:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: reliability & graceful degradation - Acme Retail

Thanks Ben — solid recap, appreciate the thoroughness. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Incident detail: the biggest outage was on 2025-11-27 (Black Friday). We had about 2.5 hours of degraded responses and then ~3 hours of recovery while infra reprovisioned GPUs. We'll attach the incident timeline — Michael is pulling the logs now.
- Infra attendee: yes, Michael Lee (michael.lee@acmeretail.com) will join. I'll also loop in procurement (Lara Patel) if we move to pricing.
- Priority: product is asking for an SLA that covers peak retail windows. 99.9% is the target; we'll want clear fallbacks first, since we can't tolerate feature drop during promotions.

Available for follow-up: Feb 25 afternoon PST works best for Michael + me. Please send a calendar invite with agenda.

Also: we'll need SOC2 and network diagram before any private deployment discussion — do you have a checklist you can send?

Sarah
Sarah Jenkins
Head of Product, Acme Retail
sarah.jenkins@acmeretail.com

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.inference>, Michael Lee <michael.lee@acmeretail.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: reliability & graceful degradation - Acme Retail

Great — thanks for the quick turnaround, Sarah. I've scheduled a 60-min follow-up for Feb 25 at 1:00 PM PST and sent a calendar invite to you and Michael. Agenda: 1) walk architecture & incident timeline; 2) proposed fallback patterns (models/regions/cache strategies); 3) SLA options and procurement timeline.

Regarding SOC2/network diagram: we maintain a public SOC2 summary and can share our security questionnaire and network diagram under an NDA or via the secure portal. I'm attaching the SLA draft now; Vivek (cc'd) will bring technical specifics on routing/fallbacks during the call.

Mutual Action Plan (MAP) — high level:
- Week 0: Share incident timeline + infra diagram (Acme)
- Week 1: Architecture deep-dive and fallback design workshop (RDW + Acme)
- Week 2: Draft SLA and procurement estimate (RDW)
- Week 3-4: Pilot (dedicated pool or private deployment) and verification metrics (joint)

Budget/procurement: do you have a target procurement window? We've seen many customers move from POC to committed Dedicated capacity within 4-6 weeks if procurement is aligned. If you can share an expected decision date, we'll prioritize pricing and capacity planning.

Attachments: SLA-draft-20260218.pdf (again). Also linking our secure checklist: https://app.redwood.inference/security/soc2-checklist

Ben

Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
